rationale_summary: California AB 2013 contains no legislative findings preamble, so its framing emerges directly from its operative disclosure categories in the Civil Code. Its dominant rationale aligns with fundamental rights—specifically personal-data privacy under California Consumer Privacy Act definitions, intellectual property ownership and licensing transparency, and public accountability over dataset provenance. Consumer and public safety forms a substantial secondary rationale, as the law mandates public-facing website disclosures for all generative AI systems made publicly available to Californians, requires reporting whether aggregate consumer information was used, and carves out dedicated security-and-integrity and national-airspace aviation systems to avoid disrupting operational safety functions.
